items.fact: Adapters (Houlsby 2019): bottleneck MLPs between layers; adds inference latency (sequential); superseded by LoRA which merges away

items.fact: Soft prompts: virtual-token embeddings prepended (prompt tuning) or to every layer's keys/values (prefix tuning, P-tuning v2)

items.fact: Soft prompts: zero architecture change, tiny counts; weaker and fiddlier than LoRA; niche today
items.where: Reading, The methods, item 3 (with DoRA Table 1's prefix 64.6 against LoRA 74.7)

items.fact: With all layers and enough capacity, LoRA matches full fine-tuning for typical post-training datasets (the low-regret regime)

items.fact: Roughly 2/3 the FLOPs (no gradient for frozen weights)

items.fact: Optimal LR ~10x the full fine-tuning LR, consistently across SFT and RL

items.fact: LoRA dislikes very large batches (effective batch < 32 best in their SFT setups); raising rank does not fix this

items.fact: For RL even rank 1 suffices: ~1 bit per episode against O(tokens) bits for SFT; capacity rarely binding; LoRA the default for RL
items.where: Reading, Against full fine-tuning (320,000 bits against 3M, recomputed 2.62M); Choosing

items.fact: Worked instance: 4B Postgres query-planner model, SFT on 420 trajectories distilled from GPT-6 Astra, LoRA ~21M parameters, consumer GPUs, anchored GRPO on execution-time reward, beat a hand-tuned production planner on join-heavy queries for a few hundred dollars
items.where: Reading, Against full fine-tuning, worked-instance box and correction box
items.status: corrected: $1,200 not a few hundred dollars; trained on a rented 2 x H100 node (3090s for development); compared with PostgreSQL's built-in planner (1.81x geometric mean, best of 3, 113 queries); 400 for training (100 + 300 of 440 generated; 420 was wrong) and 21.2M confirmed

items.fact: Capacity limit real for large-corpus training; continued pretraining scale: use full fine-tuning

items.fact: Choosing: 1 node, fits in bf16 -> LoRA all layers r=16-64, FSDP2 if sharding needed

items.fact: Choosing: GPU-poor, big base -> QLoRA (NF4 base + bf16 adapters)
items.where: Reading, Choosing table row 2

items.fact: Choosing: RL fine-tuning (GRPO etc.) -> LoRA, low rank fine
items.where: Reading, Choosing table row 3

items.fact: Choosing: domain adaptation on billions of tokens -> full fine-tuning / continued pretraining
items.where: Reading, Choosing table row 4

items.fact: Choosing: many tenants/tasks on one deployment -> per-task LoRA adapters, multi-LoRA serving
items.where: Reading, Choosing table row 5

items.fact: Quantized bases with adapters usually merged then re-quantized, or served with adapter separate to avoid quantization error on merged weights
